doc_description: Ulta Beauty, Inc.’s Fiscal 2022 Form 10-K (year ended January 28, 2023; filed March 24, 2023) detailing the largest U.S. specialty beauty retailer’s 1,355-store, omnichannel and Ulta Beauty at Target model (25,000+ SKUs; 95%+ of sales from Ultamate Rewards), key risks (macroeconomy, Project SOAR/IT, supply chain, cybersecurity, competition), and audited results of $10.21B net sales and $1.24B net income alongside significant share repurchases.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- Ulta Beauty, Inc. filed its Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended January 28, 2023.
- Company details: Delaware corporation (EIN 38-4022268), principal offices in Bolingbrook, IL; common stock (par $0.01) trades on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under ticker ULTA.
- Filing status and compliance: well-known seasoned issuer; large accelerated filer; has filed required reports and Interactive Data Files; auditor attestation of internal control over financial reporting under SOX 404(b); not a shell company; not an emerging growth or smaller reporting company.
- Share and market data: aggregate market value of non-affiliate holdings approximately $16.1 billion as of July 29, 2022; 50,195,089 shares outstanding as of March 20, 2023.
- Documents incorporated by reference: Part III information to be provided in the 2023 Proxy Statement to be filed within 120 days of fiscal year-end.
- Table of contents outlines all standard Form 10-K sections: Business; Risk Factors; Properties; Legal Proceedings; Executive Officers; Market for Common Equity and Issuer Purchases; MD&A; Market Risk; Financial Statements; Controls and Procedures; Other Information; Foreign Jurisdictions that Prevent Inspections; and Part IV Exhibits and 10-K Summary.
- Forward-looking statements section provides safe harbor disclosure and identifies key risks and uncertainties affecting future results.
- Highlighted risks include: macroeconomic pressures (inflation, interest rates, recession concerns, labor and shipping costs, COVID-19 impacts); consumer spending volatility and geopolitical events; execution of growth and operational priorities (including Project SOAR ERP and supply chain optimization); ability to identify and react to beauty trends; intense competition; distribution and fast-fulfillment center disruptions; cybersecurity and IT disruptions (including website/app reliability); privacy and data protection compliance; relationships with brand partners and exclusivity; product cost changes and vendor interruptions; impacts from epidemics/pandemics or natural disasters; real estate/developer and co-tenant risks affecting store openings; attraction and retention of key executives; climate change impacts on operations/supply chain; execution of stock repurchase programs; and potential asset impairments/store closure charges.
- The filing also includes new checkboxes regarding error corrections and any related executive compensation clawback assessments, both indicated as not applicable in this report.

structure.heading: Forward Looking Statements
structure.start_phrase:
References in this Annual Report on Form 10-K to “we,” “us,” “our,” “Ulta Beauty,” the “Company” and similar references mean Ulta
Beauty, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, unless otherwise expressly stated or the context otherwise requires.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Excerpts from Ulta Beauty’s Form 10-K, including the forward-looking statements section and the Business overview (Item 1).
- Forward-looking statements: Defines safe-harbor language and notes no obligation to update. Highlights numerous risks and uncertainties, including:
  - Macroeconomic pressures (inflation, interest rates, recession risk), labor, transportation/shipping costs, and lingering COVID-19 impacts; consumer spending volatility and geopolitical events.
  - Execution risks tied to growth plans, long-range strategy, operational excellence initiatives (continuous improvement, Project SOAR ERP replacement, supply chain optimization).
  - Market and merchandising risks (tracking beauty trends, intense competition, wholesale cost changes, vendor/brand partner disruptions, ability to maintain exclusive offerings).
  - Operational risks (distribution/fast-fulfillment center interruptions; information systems, website, and app disruptions; cybersecurity/data privacy compliance).
  - Real estate and development risks (new store openings, developer/co-tenant issues).
  - Talent, climate change impacts, future epidemics/natural disasters.
  - Capital allocation and financial risks (stock repurchase execution, potential impairments/store closures).
  - Cross-reference to additional SEC risk factor disclosures.
- Business overview:
  - Positioning: Largest specialty beauty retailer in the U.S., premier destination across cosmetics, fragrance, skincare, haircare, and salon services.
  - Assortment: 25,000+ products from 600+ established and emerging brands across prestige and mass categories, including professional hair products and tools.
  - Store footprint: 1,350+ stores in convenient, high-traffic locations with flexible layouts; most offer full-service salons and Benefit Brow Bars. 350+ Ulta Beauty at Target shop-in-shops (~1,000 sq. ft.) with curated prestige assortments.
  - Digital experiences: Ulta.com and mobile apps provide personalized, interactive shopping; omnichannel fulfillment (BOPIS, curbside, ship-from-store/DC, same-day delivery); AR and AI tools for virtual try-on and skin analysis.
  - Loyalty: Ultamate Rewards drives 95%+ of sales; points on products, services, and co-branded/private label credit cards, including purchases at Ulta Beauty at Target; robust CRM enables personalization and partner support.
  - Guest experience: Emphasis on welcoming, knowledgeable associates and engaging, relevant content to build strong guest relationships.
  - Heritage and target customer: Unique model unifying prestige, mass, and salon offerings; targets “beauty enthusiasts” who represent ~65% of shoppers and account for 80%+ of U.S. beauty spend.

structure.heading: Part I
structure.start_phrase:
Ulta Beauty is the largest specialty beauty retailer in the United States and the premier beauty destination for cosmetics, fragrance, skin care

structure.summary:
- Company overview: Ulta Beauty is the largest U.S. specialty beauty retailer and a premier destination for cosmetics, fragrance, skincare, haircare, and salon services.
- Differentiated assortment: 25,000+ products from 600+ established and emerging brands spanning prestige and mass categories, including professional hair products and tools.
- Store footprint and services: 1,350+ stores in high-traffic locations with flexible, open designs; beauty services in nearly every store (full-service hair salons and Benefit Brow Bars).
- Retail partnerships: 350+ Ulta Beauty at Target shop-in-shops offering a curated prestige assortment in 1,000 sq. ft. spaces within select Target locations.
- Digital experiences and fulfillment: Ulta.com and mobile apps deliver personalized, interactive shopping; omnichannel fulfillment (BOPIS, curbside, ship from store/DC, same-day delivery); AR/AI tools for virtual try-on and skin analysis.
- Loyalty program: Ultamate Rewards enables members to earn and redeem points across products and services, credit cards, and Target shop-in-shops; 95%+ of sales from members; robust CRM-driven personalization supporting brand partner growth.
- Guest experience focus: Emphasis on welcoming, knowledgeable service and compelling digital content to deepen engagement.
- History and market positioning: Founded in 1990 to unify prestige, mass, and salon offerings in one specialty format; targets “beauty enthusiasts” (about 65% of shoppers) who drive over 80% of U.S. beauty spend.

structure.title: Business
structure.heading: Item 1. Business
structure.start_phrase: Ulta Beauty is the largest specialty beauty retailer in the United States and the premier beauty destination for cosmetics, fragrance, skin care products, hair care products, and salon services.
structure.summary:
- Company overview: Ulta Beauty is the largest specialty beauty retailer in the U.S., offering a one-of-a-kind, 25,000+ SKU assortment across 600+ brands and price points, salon services, and leading digital experiences. Competitive strengths include a nationwide store footprint (1,355 stores at FY22-end), best-in-class loyalty (95% of sales from 40.2M active members), and strong guest experiences across channels.
- Target consumer and history: Serves “beauty enthusiasts,” who represent ~65% of shoppers and over 80% of U.S. beauty spend. Ulta pioneered a specialty concept uniting prestige, mass, and salon products/services in one destination.
- Strategy (six pillars):
  - Drive disruptive growth via “All Things Beauty” by maximizing core categories (makeup, skincare, haircare, fragrance), scaling cross-category platforms (Conscious Beauty, BIPOC-founded brands, Wellness Shop, SPARKED), exclusives/private label, and profitability levers.
  - Evolve omnichannel “All In Your World” through connected stores and digital, expanded services, and buy/fill-anywhere capabilities.
  - Deepen role “At the Heart of the Beauty Community” by amplifying brand purpose, creator/content ecosystem, loyalty innovation, and data-driven personalization.
  - Operational excellence: continuous improvement, ERP upgrade (Project SOAR), supply chain agility/cost efficiency.
  - Culture and talent: attract/retain/develop associates; values-based, high-performance culture.
  - Environmental and social impact: inclusivity, Conscious Beauty transparency, and environmental footprint reduction.
- Market: U.S. beauty products ($104B) and salon services ($68B) markets in 2022; Ulta estimates ~9% share of beauty products and <1% of salon services.
- Competition: Department/specialty stores, grocery/drug/mass retailers, brand DTC/online, pure-play e-commerce, and fragmented salon providers.
- Retail channels:
  - Stores: Predominantly power strip centers; typical 10,000 sq. ft. with full-service salons and brow bars; new layout organizes by category from prestige to mass and adds Beauty Bars. FY22 ended with 1,355 stores; long-term potential 1,500–1,700.
  - Digital: Ulta.com and apps with virtual try-on/AI skin analysis; robust omnichannel services (BOPIS, curbside, ship-from-store/DC, same-day delivery). Omnichannel guests spend ~3x retail-only.
  - Partnerships: Ulta Beauty at Target shop-in-shops (350+ at FY22-end; goal up to 800), curated prestige assortment, loyalty points earn (not redeemable) at Target.
- Merchandising:
  - Broad, inclusive assortment across cosmetics, haircare, skincare, fragrance/bath, tools, and services; trend and diversity-forward approach.
  - Signature platforms: Conscious Beauty (clean, cruelty free, vegan, sustainable packaging) with >300 participating brands; Wellness Shop across six wellness areas.
  - Commitment to BIPOC brands; progress toward 15% assortment representation.
  - Private label (Ulta Beauty Collection) and exclusives; private label and permanent exclusives ~4% of FY22 sales; all exclusives (perm + temp) ~10%.
  - Sales mix FY22: Cosmetics 42%; Haircare/tools 21%; Skincare 17%; Fragrance/bath 14%; Services 3%; Accessories/other 3%.
- Merchandising operations: Centralized org structure (CIO, SVPs/VPs, DMMs, buyers), planograms, visual standards, and disciplined planning/open-to-buy process using POS data; weekly inventory productivity oversight.
- Brand partnerships: Top 10 partners ~56% of FY22 sales; vendor standards and sustainable packaging goal (50% recyclable/refillable/recycled/bio-sourced by 2025).
- Marketing and loyalty:
  - Multi-channel marketing (print, TV/radio, digital/social/streaming) to drive awareness and traffic.
  - Ultamate Rewards loyalty and co-brand/private-label credit cards to increase spend, retention, and insights.
  - Expanded gift card distribution.
  - Retail media network (UB Media) launched May 2022 to monetize audience/data and support brand partners.
- Operations and staffing:
  - Store staffing model (GM-led teams; licensed salon pros; extended holiday hours).
  - Salon education for ~6,800 professionals.
- Supply chain: Four DCs (store + e-comm), two fast-fulfillment (e-comm), 115 ship-from-store locations; launching market fulfillment centers from 2023 for high-density markets; replenishment in eaches; broad carrier network.
- Human capital:
  - ~53,000 associates (18.5k full-time; 34.5k part-time); focus on engagement, culture, and development with majority internal promotions.
  - DEI integrated across recruitment, training, and guest experience; recurring inclusion training.
  - Representation (as of FY22): Women 55% of Board/66% leadership/91% associates; People of color 36% Board/27% leadership/53% associates.
  - Governance by CHRO/executive team and Board committees; regular engagement surveys and forums.
  - Benefits: Health coverage, 401(k) match, disability/life, tuition reimbursement, PTO, discounts, wellness/mental health resources, Associate Relief Program.
- Sustainability: Store energy/water efficiency, safe indoor air, renewable energy credits, collaboration with brand partners on Scope 3 reductions.
- Information technology and cybersecurity: Integrated systems (including cloud); board-level cyber oversight; SOC monitoring, layered defenses, training; multi-year ERP upgrade for scalability and efficiency.
- Intellectual property: Extensive ULTA-related trademarks (U.S. and select international), including key branded taglines and programs.
- Regulation: Compliance with FDA, FTC, CPSC, EPA, and state/local rules across product categories and salon licensing; advertising/claims oversight; labor/employment and real estate permitting.
- Seasonality: Strongest in Q4 holiday period; secondary lifts around Mother’s Day and Valentine’s Day.
- Investor information access: Reports available on ulta.com/investor and SEC.gov; forward-looking statements caveat.
- Risk highlights (excerpt):
  - Potential inability to sustain growth and execute strategic/operational initiatives (e.g., continuous improvement, ERP replacement, supply chain optimization).
  - Risk of misreading beauty trends/consumer preferences (including sustainability/ingredient transparency/animal welfare), vendor access to newness, and inventory/markdown pressures.

structure.title: Risk Factors
structure.heading: Item 1A. Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase: The risks described below could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, or future growth.
structure.summary:
- Available information and disclosures
  - Company provides SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, proxy) free on its investor relations site and via SEC.gov; website information not incorporated by reference.
  - Forward-looking statements are made as of their dates; no obligation to update unless required by law.

- Item 1A. Risk Factors
  - Business, operational and strategic risks
    - Ability to execute long-range strategies and growth plans, including Project SOAR (ERP replacement), supply chain optimization, and continuous improvement.
    - Dependence on forecasting beauty trends and shifting consumer preferences (sustainability, ingredient transparency, animal welfare), vendor relationships, and in-stock/distribution efficiency.
    - Vulnerability to distribution and fast fulfillment center interruptions; rising shipping/transportation costs.
    - Omnichannel/e-commerce risks: potential store cannibalization, channel conflicts, vendor distribution changes, heightened competition, and need to deliver timely guest-facing technology.
    - Overseas sourcing risks (imports, tariffs, geopolitical events, labor disputes, disease, disasters, war/terrorism); lack of long-term supply contracts; potential increased costs and disruptions.
    - Reliance on brand partner relationships, capacity, and exclusivity; vendor consolidation and concentration (top ten vendors ~56% of net sales in 2022).
    - Elevated inventory shrink (damage, theft, organized retail crime) and potential negative impacts of mitigation actions.
    - Comparable sales and quarterly volatility due to economic conditions, merchandising mix, store performance, openings/cannibalization, marketing timing, seasonality, competition, and disasters.
    - Distribution capacity may be insufficient to support growth; need for timely expansion to avoid excess costs and service failures.
    - Marketing/advertising effectiveness across digital, social, and traditional media; potential channel disruptions.
    - Social media risks (reputation, rapid amplification, evolving compliance requirements).
    - Talent and labor pressures: retention of senior management, hiring/training across the organization, wage inflation.
    - Credit facility covenants ($1.0B secured revolver to March 2025) may restrict flexibility; collateralized; financial covenant triggers if availability declines.
  - Economic, market and external risks
    - Macroeconomic pressures (inflation, interest rates, recession concerns, labor/supply chain/shipping costs, banking turmoil); Russia-Ukraine conflict exacerbating inflation.
    - Sensitivity of discretionary spending on beauty and salon services to economic conditions; potential partner (vendor/landlord) financial distress.
    - Intense competition across retail formats and online; larger competitors may have resource advantages.
    - Dependence on co-tenant traffic in power centers; anchor closures or reduced traffic can depress sales and increase markdowns.
    - Ongoing and potential future impacts from COVID-19; persistent shifts in behavior and inflationary effects.
    - Future epidemics, natural disasters, terrorism could cause store/DC closures, supply disruptions, workforce shortages, higher costs.
    - Stock repurchase program risks (price effects; potential suspension; no assurance of value creation).
    - Climate change and ESG: operational disruptions from extreme weather; potential regulatory cost increases; shifting consumer preferences; reputation risk.
  - Information security, cybersecurity, privacy, regulatory and legal risks
    - Cyber/information security threats (breaches, ransomware, phishing, remote work vulnerabilities) could expose data, disrupt operations, and create liabilities.
    - IT system dependence and upgrade risks (including Project SOAR); potential e-commerce downtime and holiday-season vulnerabilities.
    - Evolving privacy/data protection laws (e.g., California and other states) increase compliance costs and risk of penalties/reputational harm.
    - Litigation and regulatory proceedings (employment, consumer, data security, contracts, IP) could be costly; loss contingencies may be inadequate; IP infringement risks may force licensing or product changes.
    - Reliance on third-party manufacturers for Ulta-branded and promotional products; need to meet FDA/other regulatory standards; noncompliance could trigger sanctions, recalls, and brand damage.
    - Broad regulatory exposure: labor/employment (minimum wage, benefits), salon licensing, California Proposition 65, healthcare reform, and product/advertising rules (FDA, FTC, CPSC, state AGs).
    - Risk of associate/contractor misconduct (policy, legal, ethical violations) and related reputational harm.
    - Protection and enforcement of trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, and digital innovations; partner licensing could affect brand if standards aren’t met.
    - Product liability risks for Ulta-branded products and salon services due to adverse effects; insurance may be insufficient.
  - Anti-takeover provisions
    - Staggered board, authority to issue preferred/extra common shares, no stockholder written consent or special meeting rights, advance notice requirements, and Delaware law restrictions may deter change in control and affect stock price.

- Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
  - None.

structure.title: Unresolved Staff Comments
structure.heading: Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments
structure.start_phrase: null.
structure.summary:
- Anti-takeover measures: The company’s certificate of incorporation and bylaws include a classified board with staggered three-year terms, authorization to issue preferred stock and additional common shares without stockholder approval, prohibitions on stockholder action by written consent and on calling special meetings, and advance notice requirements for stockholder proposals and director nominations. Delaware law (including restrictions on business combinations with 15%+ stockholders for three years) further reinforces these defenses. Collectively, these provisions may deter change-in-control transactions, depress takeover premiums, and make management removal more difficult.
- Item 1B – Unresolved Staff Comments: None.
- Properties: All retail stores, distribution centers, fast fulfillment centers, market fulfillment centers, and corporate offices are leased or subleased. Retail stores are typically ~10,000 sq. ft. (with ~950 sq. ft. salons), located in high-traffic power centers. Store leases generally have 10-year initial terms with two or three 5-year renewal options. As of January 28, 2023, the company operated 1,355 stores across all 50 U.S. states, with the largest concentrations in California (168), Texas (126), Florida (92), New York (55), Illinois (55), and Ohio/Pennsylvania (45 each).

structure.heading: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase: The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
structure.summary:
- Company overview and strategy: Ulta Beauty is the largest specialty beauty retailer in the U.S., offering 25,000+ products, salon services, and omnichannel experiences (Ulta.com and mobile apps) supported by a leading loyalty program. Target customer is the “beauty enthusiast.” Strategic priorities include expanding “All Things Beauty,” advancing omnichannel (“All In Your World”), deepening community engagement, driving operational excellence, investing in culture and talent, and growing environmental/social impact. Long-term plan targets 1,500–1,700 U.S. stores, comp growth, and omnichannel expansion.

- Key operating metric: Comparable sales (retail, salon, and e‑commerce) with methodology and factors that influence comps (economic environment, new brands, store overlap, competition, consumer preferences, marketing, and store age).

- Basis of presentation and revenue recognition: Single reportable segment. Merchandise revenue recognized at point of sale; e‑commerce upon shipment/guest pickup; salon at service time; gift cards deferred until redemption; coupons reduce net sales. Other revenue includes private label/co‑brand credit cards, Target partnership royalties, loyalty program deferrals, and gift card breakage.

- Cost structure definitions:
  - Cost of sales includes merchandise costs (net of certain vendor income), distribution, shipping/handling, store occupancy, salon payroll/benefits, and shrink/inventory reserves.
  - SG&A includes store/corporate payroll and benefits, advertising/marketing (net of specific vendor reimbursements), corporate occupancy, stock-based comp, corporate depreciation/amortization, and other overhead.
  - Separate lines for impairment/restructuring, pre-opening, interest (income)/expense, and income taxes.

- Current trends and risks:
  - COVID‑19: No apparent negative impact in fiscal 2022 but ongoing uncertainties (operations, supply chain, costs, labor).
  - Industry: Market share gains across categories; beauty market rebounded through 2022; confidence in model and investments.
  - Macroeconomy: Inflation and other trends could pressure consumer spending, margins, SG&A leverage, and future interest costs.

- Results of operations (fiscal years ended Jan 28, 2023; Jan 29, 2022; Jan 30, 2021):
  - Scale and performance: Net sales $10.21B/$8.63B/$6.15B; gross margin 39.6%/39.0%/31.7%; SG&A as % of sales 23.5%/23.9%/25.7%; operating margin 16.1%/15.0%/3.9%; net income $1,242M/$986M/$176M.
  - Store base/comps: 1,355 stores at FY22 end; comps +15.6% in 2022, +37.9% in 2021, −17.9% in 2020.
  - FY22 vs FY21: Net sales +$1.6B on category resilience, price increases, new brands/innovation, more social occasions, and +$77M other revenue; comps driven by transactions (+10.8%) and ticket (+4.3%). Gross margin +60 bps (fixed cost leverage +100 bps; other revenue +60 bps; channel mix +20 bps; offset by shrink −70 bps; merchandise margin −50 bps). SG&A leveraged −40 bps net (lower marketing and incentive comp leverage offset by higher corporate investments and wage investments). Interest swung to income; ETR 24.4%. Net income +$257M.
  - FY21 vs FY20: Net sales +$2.5B on recovery and easing COVID restrictions; comps +37.9% (transactions +30%, ticket +6%). Gross margin +730 bps (fixed cost leverage, lower promos/cost optimization, channel mix, salon leverage). SG&A leveraged 180 bps despite lower CARES credits and higher incentives. No FY21 impairments vs $114M in FY20. ETR 23.9%. Net income +$810M.

- Liquidity and capital resources: Liquidity from cash, operations, and an undrawn ABL facility. Cash and equivalents $737.9M (FY22) vs $431.6M (FY21). Working capital peaks Aug–Nov for holiday inventory.

- Contractual obligations (undiscounted): Operating leases ~$2.21B (including ~$91.5M leases signed not commenced); purchase obligations ~$111M; total ~$2.32B.

- Cash flows (FY22/FY21/FY20): Operating $1,482M/$1,059M/$810M; Investing $(315)M/$(176)M/$(49)M; Financing $(861)M/$(1,497)M/$(108)M. Operating cash up on higher earnings and inventory/receivables timing; inventory up ~$104M (new stores, brand launches, cost increases). Investing cash use up on higher capex. Financing use down due to lower share repurchases.

- Capital expenditures and store activity:
  - FY22 capex $312M (new/remodel/relocate stores, IT, supply chain, maintenance). FY23 plan up to $475M (stores, IT, supply chain).
  - FY22 openings/remodels/relocations: 47/20/12; average new store investment ~$1.7M.

- Share repurchases: 2020 authorization $1.6B; 2022 authorization $2.0B (superseded prior remaining). Repurchases: FY22 2.19M shares for $900M; FY21 4.25M for $1.52B; FY20 0.47M for $114.9M.

- Credit facility: ABL maturing Mar 11, 2025; up to $1.0B (plus possible $100M increase), $50M LC subfacility, asset-based borrowing base, FCCR covenant if availability drops. Rates: base +0%–0.125% or LIBOR +1.125%–1.25%; 0.20% unused fee. Substantially all assets pledged. No borrowings outstanding FY20–FY22.

- Seasonality: Heaviest sales and profits in Q4 (holiday); also impacted by Mother’s Day and Valentine’s Day.

- Critical accounting policies/estimates: Inventory valuation and shrink; vendor allowances; impairment of long‑lived assets; loyalty program revenue deferral and redemption estimates; income taxes (deferred taxes, uncertain tax positions). Sensitivity analyses indicate no material impacts from reasonable estimate changes.

- Market risk (Item 7A): Exposure primarily to variable interest rates on potential credit facility borrowings; no outstanding debt.

- Other items: Reference to audited financial statements; no changes/disagreements with accountants; disclosure controls deemed effective as of Jan 28, 2023; management responsible for internal control over financial reporting.

- Independent auditor’s reports (Ernst & Young LLP, PCAOB ID 42):
  - Unqualified opinion on the consolidated financial statements for fiscal years ended January 28, 2023; January 29, 2022; and January 30, 2021.
  - Unqualified opinion on internal control over financial reporting as of January 28, 2023, under COSO (2013).
  - Critical audit matter: accounting for the loyalty program (Ultamate Rewards), focusing on deferred revenue recognition, standalone selling price per point, and expected redemption rates; summary of audit procedures addressing data completeness, assumptions, methodology, and sensitivity analyses.

- Consolidated financial statements:
  - Balance sheets: Total assets $5.37B (2023) vs $4.76B (2022); significant operating lease assets and liabilities; stockholders’ equity $1.96B; no outstanding debt; cash and cash equivalents $738M.
  - Income statements: Net sales $10.21B (2023), $8.63B (2022), $6.15B (2021); gross profit $4.04B (2023); operating income $1.64B (2023); net income $1.24B (2023); diluted EPS $24.01 (2023).
  - Comprehensive income: minimal foreign currency impact.
  - Cash flows: Operating cash flow $1.48B (2023); capital expenditures $312M; share repurchases $900M; ending cash $738M.
  - Stockholders’ equity changes: impacts of stock-based compensation, option exercises, treasury share purchases, and repurchases.

- Notes to consolidated financial statements (key areas):
  - Business overview: specialty beauty retailer with 1,355 U.S. stores; one reportable segment (retail, salon services, e-commerce).
  - Significant accounting policies: fiscal year definition; consolidation; use of estimates (inventory, vendor allowances, long-lived asset impairment, loyalty program, income taxes); cash equivalents; receivables (including ERC); vendor allowances; inventory valuation and reserves; property & equipment and internal-use software; cloud computing arrangements; impairment of long-lived and ROU assets; goodwill and other intangibles; leases (recognition, discount rate, variable lease costs); loyalty program revenue deferral; private-label and co-branded credit card arrangements; gift card accounting and breakage; revenue recognition model; advertising expense (3.7% of net sales in 2023); pre-opening expenses; cost of sales and SG&A components; income taxes (deferreds, uncertain tax positions); stock-based compensation; insurance programs; net income per share.
  - Revenue (disaggregation): category mix—cosmetics (42%), haircare (21%), skincare (17%), fragrance/bath (14%), services (3%), accessories/other (3%); deferred revenue rollforward for loyalty points and gift cards.
  - Impairment, restructuring, and other costs: primarily fiscal 2020 COVID-19-related charges (store impairments/closures; suspension of Canadian expansion); none in fiscal 2022 or 2021.
  - Prepaid expenses/other assets: cloud computing costs and amortization.
  - Property & equipment: components and accumulated depreciation.
  - Goodwill: stable at $10.9M; no acquisitions.
  - Other intangibles: developed technology amortization and remaining expense schedule.
  - Leases: operating leases only; ROU assets $1.56B; lease liabilities $1.90B; weighted-average remaining term 6.7 years; discount rate 3.2%; annual lease costs and cash payments; lease maturity schedule and not-yet-commenced commitments.
  - Commitments and contingencies: $111M non-cancelable obligations (supply chain and IT); litigation not material.
  - Accrued liabilities detail (payroll/benefits, taxes, capex, advertising).
  - Income taxes: provision detail; effective tax rate ~24.4% (2023); deferred tax assets/liabilities (notably lease-related); IRA 2022 effects (CAMT and 1% buyback excise) not material; uncertain tax positions rollforward; tax audit status.
  - Debt: $1.0B asset-based revolving credit facility maturing 2025; no borrowings outstanding; covenant compliance.
  - Fair value measurements: hierarchy definitions; Level 2 deferred compensation plan liabilities.
  - Investments: equity-method renewable energy investments; other strategic investments.
  - Stock-based compensation: plan description and award types (options, RSUs, PBSs); expense by award type; option valuation assumptions (Black-Scholes); outstanding/vested options; RSU and PBS activity; unrecognized compensation expense.
  - Net income per share: basic/diluted share reconciliations and anti-dilutive awards.
  - Employee benefit plans: 401(k) match and non-qualified deferred compensation plan; related expenses and balances.
  - Share repurchase programs: 2020 and 2022 authorizations; shares repurchased and total cost in fiscal 2021–2023.
